Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BIOLOGY
Strand: Anatomy and Physiology of Animals
Topic 3.2: Transport
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Transport, part of Anatomy and Physiology of Animals in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 BIOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: Why is transport important in animals? 2. How do transport systems in animals differ?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Transport together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner analyses the compatibility of blood donor and recipient for safe

transfusion of blood.

• Self-efficacy: The learner exhibits confidence and self-esteem during dissection of a small mammal to examine the

transport system.

Values:
• Love: The learner respects others while searching and discussing information on the transport system of mammals.

• Peace: The learner displays tolerance towards other group members while carrying out the dissection of mammals.

Suggested learning resources

Adapted writing materials, pair of forceps, dissecting kit, mounting needles, virtual labs, medical laboratory technician,

chart on blood donor-recipient compatibility, small animal, animations on blood clot,
